description:
When a case's subject type already decides a test, the native lowering still emits the test, and still emits a miss arm that cannot be reached.

Repro (base 81c747daf): `case a == 1 do true -> false; false -> true end`. The subject is typed :false|:true, so after `equal(true)` fails the remainder is :false, the `equal(false)` test is settled, and the miss is impossible. The lowered code still has both compares and a `halt :case_clause` block. After fz-sc8.37, every `and`/`or`/`not` (which lower to a case with a BadBooleanError/ArgumentError miss) pays two compares and a halt block the same way: `a == 1 or a == 2` under --dump backend= shows `test equal(true)`, `test equal(false)`, then fail with `halt :BadBooleanError`.

Mechanism (builder's reading, to be re-verified by the reader): jobs/native.rs lower_dispatch_test settles a question statically only through settled_lane_form_type_test (tuples held as lanes). An atom `equal(..)` region is never settled by the subject's type, and the DoesNotHold proofs on a miss edge are not used to narrow. executable_facts.rs treats miss_entry as always reachable.

Done when: a test that observes the dispatch plan or telemetry, not text output, shows that a boolean-typed `or`/`and`/`not` and the hand-written exhaustive case lower with no reachable halt and no settled test. Interp, run and build agree. The pins fz-sc8.37 raised for this cause (blind-escape census case row 3->11, join walk 29->38, membership `main/0`) come back down; any other movement is explained. Proposal page first. Worked right after fz-sc8.37 lands (decided 2026-10-24).

Acceptance: pins raised by fz-sc8.37 for this cause come back down (decided 2026-10-24). Each pin below returns to its pre-fz-sc8.37 value or lower. Any pin that stays above that value is explained entry by entry with a measured mechanism and approved; it is never re-blessed quietly.
- drive_test.rs compiler2_dispatch_blind_escape_census_is_the_known_population: ("case", 11, 11) -> ("case", 3, 3). The 8 entries fz-sc8.37 added are Map.member_pair?/5 (00277 and map_enumerable x2), Range.contains?/4 (00277 x2, range_enumerable x2) and Enum.reject/2#lambda@0/1 (00569).
- drive_test.rs compiler2_join_walk_visits_each_entry_and_scope_once: resume entries 38 -> 29, type-analysis walk 48 -> 34, runtime-demand walk 37 -> 28, executable-facts walk 38 -> 29.
- drive_test.rs compiler2_membership_operator_protocol_receivers_settle_to_direct_impls: ["Kernel.===/2", "main/0"] -> ["Kernel.===/2"]. The `dbg(not m)` per-literal dispatch goes away once the `not` result is not a literal union built from a dead case.
- The 34 pins fz-sc8.37 raised for the Kernel macro definitions (cause M) are not expected to move. If any of them does, explain it.
- The hand-written exhaustive `case a == 1 do true -> false; false -> true end` loses its `halt :case_clause` block. This is checked by the same telemetry or plan test that checks `or`/`and`/`not`.

Design: page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.44.html, APPROVED 2026-10-24, with the recommended census rule (the census counts only plans that still decide something at runtime). Dispatch reachability (calculate_dispatch_reachability) is the single authority: per activation it records which test nodes the type settles and whether fail is reachable, folded into the walk type analysis already does. Readers: the semantic.rs:1141 miss join, native lower_dispatch_test/control-dispatch fail, executable_facts (:782, :1121), runtime_demand (:1626), artifact (:1452). The interp evaluates every test and reports a loud internal error on reaching a fail that has no miss entry. Shape-only settlers are deleted where the type answer covers them; any kept is justified by a probe. Telemetry: activation_analysis gains settled-test and unreachable-fail counts.
title: A case skips a test its subject's type already answers, and builds no miss it cannot reach
